title: Are They Ready to Teach? Generative AI as a Means to Uncover Pre-Service Science Teachers’ PCK and Enhance Their Preparation Program
venue: Journal of Science Education and Technology
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the challenge of assessing and developing pre-service science teachers’ pedagogical content knowledge (PCK) during teacher preparation. The authors argue that generative AI (GenAI) can be used not only as a planning aid but also as a diagnostic tool that reveals what prospective teachers know about content, pedagogy, and the integration of both while they work through lesson planning tasks.

The proposed approach centers on recording pre-service teachers’ conversations with a GenAI system during lesson design, then having trained GenAI evaluate the dialogue for evidence of content knowledge, pedagogical knowledge, and PCK. The paper is conceptual rather than empirical: it illustrates the idea through example ChatGPT dialogues in chemistry, including one with an experienced educator and one with a pre-service teacher. These examples show how prompts and follow-up questions can expose the teacher’s level of understanding, including gaps related to classroom management, subject-specific teaching strategies, and lesson design.

The intended population is pre-service science teachers in initial teacher education, with examples grounded in chemistry education. The broader context is teacher preparation programs that aim to personalize instruction, support self-regulated learning, and strengthen future teachers’ ability to use GenAI responsibly and effectively. The authors conclude that GenAI dialogue analysis could help personalize teacher education and support formative assessment of PCK, but they caution that AI evaluations can be overly optimistic and should be checked by human educators and validated against established PCK assessment methods.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI conversational assistant / large language model chatbot used for interactive dialogue, content generation, and feedback/evaluation tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Used in a conceptual paper to analyze pre-service science teachers’ lesson-planning dialogues as a way to reveal and evaluate PCK, and illustrated with example chats about molecular vs. ionic materials.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a conceptual/theoretical paper with illustrative examples, not an empirical evaluation of an AI tool. No study design, sample, or outcome data are reported.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper argues that ChatGPT could support lesson planning, PCK diagnosis, and personalization, but it does not provide empirical effect estimates. Impact is therefore speculative rather than measured.
